newsitem.title: USA: Federal Signal net below long-term goal.
newsitem.headline: Federal Signal net below long-term goal.

text.p: Federal Signal Corp, which earlier reported higher third-quarter results, said Thursday that earnings growth this year has been below its long-term goal, but it should be back on track in 1997.

"Our 1996 earnings growth has been strong yet below our long-term targeted level," said Joseph Ross, chairman, president and chief executive. "We believe the foundation is in place for a return to our long-term earnings growth goal in 1997."
Federal Signal earlier said it earned $15.9 million, or $0.35 a share, in the third quarter versus $14.6 million, or $0.32, in the same period last year.

The company said all four of its groups posted higher sales and earnings, and its Vehicle and Tool groups had the strongest performances. Orders for the third quarter rose 28 percent over last year, led by increases at the Vehicle Group.

The group's earnings rose 17 percent in the quarter on a sales gain of five percent. Orders were up 40 percent, Federal Signal said. Strong orders earlier this year at Emergency One added to strength in fire apparatus sales and earnings.

Fire apparatus orders rose more than 70 percent over last year's third quarter with gains at both Emergency One and Bronto, the company said. In addition to increased market strength, Bronto's restructured focus on the fire market enabled it to post an operating profit following losses in the first two quarters of this year.

"We have dealt with a weak Bronto, two weak market sectors in the Safety Products Group, and a weak European vehicle market," Ross said. "We continue to be challenged in the current quarter, both by the impact of market issues earlier in the year as well as by short-term mix issues in both our Safety Products and Vehicle groups. At the same time, market weaknesses appear to be improving, early results from the Bronto and Ravo restructurings are very encouraging, and we are excited about the prospects for new products."
